900100.title: The Time Traveler's Ball
900100.description: Every era, one room: the time-travel theme.
900100.content:
The Time Traveler's Ball — Every era, one room: the time-travel theme.

The time traveler's ball invites every era to one room: guests dress from any century, and the party becomes a collision of histories. The design key is the era stations — a roaring twenties corner, a medieval feast table, a neon eighties dance floor — so the theme is explorable, not just wearable. The activity is the era quiz: teams identify the century from the costume clues. The hosting craft is the timeline arch at the entrance — guests walk through time to arrive. The ball's lesson: the best themes are frameworks, not costumes. Give the guests a structure and they'll fill it with centuries.

Key points:
- Era stations make the theme explorable.
- Costume clues drive the era quiz.
- The timeline arch sets the entrance.
- Themes are frameworks, not costumes.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Time Traveler's Ball

900101.title: The Neon Noir Night
900101.description: Detective shadows in neon: the noir party.
900101.content:
The Neon Noir Night — Detective shadows in neon: the noir party.

The neon noir night is detective fiction with the lights turned electric: fedoras and trench coats under blacklight, the case file as the evening's game. The design key is the lighting — blacklight, neon tape, and fog turn any room into a 1940s fever dream. The game is the case: teams get evidence envelopes and thirty minutes to name the culprit. The hosting craft is the saxophone playlist and the venetian-blind shadows. The noir night's lesson: atmosphere is a game mechanic. Light the room right and the guests play along.

Key points:
- Blacklight and fog make the noir.
- The case file is the evening's game.
- Venetian-blind shadows sell it.
- Atmosphere is a game mechanic.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Neon Noir Night

900102.title: The Enchanted Forest Feast
900102.description: Moss, lanterns, and long tables: the forest feast.
900102.content:
The Enchanted Forest Feast — Moss, lanterns, and long tables: the forest feast.

The enchanted forest feast brings the woods indoors: moss runners, lantern light, and a long table that seats everyone together. The design key is the canopy — drape the ceiling with greenery and the room becomes a glade. The menu is the forest: mushrooms, berries, game, and bread baked like the old stories. The activity is the tale round: each guest tells a two-minute story, true or invented. The feast's lesson: the long table is the theme — one table, no head, everyone equal under the lanterns. The forest is the feeling; the table is the point.

Key points:
- Canopy the ceiling with greenery.
- The menu is the forest.
- Tale rounds: two-minute stories.
- One long table, no head.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Enchanted Forest Feast

900103.title: The Retro Arcade Party
900103.description: Quarters and high scores: the arcade night.
900103.content:
The Retro Arcade Party — Quarters and high scores: the arcade night.

The retro arcade party runs on quarters and high scores: rented cabinets, a tournament bracket, and a prize table of pure nostalgia. The design key is the tournament — seed the bracket, run the heats, and crown the champion before midnight. The decor is the glow: neon, pixel art, and the cabinet marquees do the decorating. The hosting craft is the free-play hour before the bracket — let the guests warm up. The arcade party's lesson: competition is the theme's engine. The cabinets are the excuse; the bracket is the party.

Key points:
- Run a real tournament bracket.
- Cabinet glow does the decorating.
- Free-play hour before competition.
- Competition is the theme's engine.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Retro Arcade Party

900104.title: The Masquerade of Masks
900104.content:
The Masquerade of Masks — Identity optional: the masquerade ball.

The masquerade ball makes identity optional: masks at the door, names left with the coats, and the evening runs on mystery. The design key is the unmasking — midnight, all masks off, and the room discovers who it danced with. The activity is the secret admirer: guests draw names and leave anonymous notes all night. The hosting craft is the mask-making station — the craft table is the icebreaker. The masquerade's lesson: anonymity is a social lubricant. The mask frees the guest; the unmasking bonds the room.

Key points:
- Masks at the door; unmasking at midnight.
- Secret admirer notes all night.
- The mask station is the icebreaker.
- Anonymity lubricates; unmasking bonds.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Masquerade of Masks

900105.title: The Around the World Night
900105.description: Seven countries, one evening: the world tour party.
900105.content:
The Around the World Night — Seven countries, one evening: the world tour party.

The around the world night tours seven countries in one evening: each room or table is a nation, with its food, music, and a game. The design key is the passport — guests collect stamps at each country, and the full passport enters the prize draw. The curation is the balance: one dish, one drink, one game per country — depth over sprawl. The hosting craft is the departure board: the schedule of tastings and performances. The world night's lesson: the passport is the party — the collecting gives the evening its shape. Seven stamps; one world.

Key points:
- Passports with stamps drive the tour.
- One dish, one drink, one game per country.
- The departure board schedules the night.
- Collecting gives the evening shape.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Around the World Night

900106.title: The Mad Scientist Lab
900106.description: Beakers and bubbling: the laboratory party.
900106.content:
The Mad Scientist Lab — Beakers and bubbling: the laboratory party.

The mad scientist lab turns the party into an experiment: lab coats at the door, beakers for drinks, and dry ice in the punch. The design key is the experiments — safe, spectacular demos that guests perform themselves. The decor is the lab: warning signs, chalk formulas, and bubbling flasks. The hosting craft is the safety brief — real goggles, real rules, real fun. The lab party's lesson: interactivity is the theme — the guests don't watch science, they do it. The beakers are the glasses; the guests are the scientists.

Key points:
- Guest-performed experiments.
- Lab decor: signs, formulas, flasks.
- Real safety brief, real goggles.
- Guests do science; they don't watch it.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Mad Scientist Lab

900107.title: The Hollywood Premiere
900107.description: Red carpet and flashbulbs: the premiere party.
900107.content:
The Hollywood Premiere — Red carpet and flashbulbs: the premiere party.

The Hollywood premiere rolls out the red carpet: a step-and-repeat wall, flashbulb photos, and acceptance speeches for the evening's awards. The design key is the awards — silliest categories win: best entrance, best dramatic pause, the lifetime achievement for showing up. The activity is the trailer: teams film a 60-second movie trailer on their phones and premiere it. The hosting craft is the paparazzi — a designated photographer makes everyone feel famous. The premiere's lesson: the camera is the theme — point it at the guests and they perform. The red carpet is the runway; the guests are the stars.

Key points:
- Silly awards: best entrance, best pause.
- Teams film 60-second trailers.
- A paparazzi makes everyone famous.
- Point the camera; guests perform.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Hollywood Premiere

900108.title: The Pirate Cove Party
900108.description: X marks the spot: the pirate bash.
900108.content:
The Pirate Cove Party — X marks the spot: the pirate bash.

The pirate cove party buries treasure in the backyard: a real treasure map, real clues, and a chest of prizes at the X. The design key is the hunt — the map's clues should take thirty minutes and end in triumph. The decor is the cove: nets, barrels, and a plank (for photos, not walking). The hosting craft is the pirate speak contest — judged, with a prize for the most committed arr. The cove party's lesson: the hunt is the theme — the costumes are the crew, but the map is the voyage. X marks the spot; the hunt marks the night.

Key points:
- A real 30-minute treasure hunt.
- Cove decor: nets, barrels, photo plank.
- Pirate speak contest, judged.
- The hunt is the theme.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Pirate Cove Party

900109.title: The Space Station Soirée
900109.description: Zero gravity, full elegance: the orbital party.
900109.content:
The Space Station Soirée — Zero gravity, full elegance: the orbital party.

The space station soirée hosts the party in orbit: silver and starlight, freeze-dried hors d'oeuvres, and a mission patch for every guest. The design key is the viewport — a projected Earthrise that slowly rotates all night. The activity is the mission: teams run a simulated spacewalk (a VR headset or a blindfold obstacle course). The hosting craft is the countdown — the evening launches with a ten-second countdown. The soirée's lesson: the theme is a world — commit to the bit and the guests will live in it. The station is the setting; the countdown is the start.

Key points:
- Projected Earthrise viewport.
- The mission: simulated spacewalk.
- Launch the evening with a countdown.
- Commit to the world.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Space Station Soirée

900110.title: The Tuscan Harvest Table
900110.description: Rustic abundance: the Tuscan dinner party.
900110.content:
The Tuscan Harvest Table — Rustic abundance: the Tuscan dinner party.

The Tuscan harvest table is rustic abundance: a long wooden table, family-style platters, and wine that doesn't need a special occasion. The menu arc runs antipasti, handmade pasta, the roast, and the almond cake — each course arriving when the conversation peaks. The design key is the family style: big platters passed hand to hand make strangers into tablemates. The hosting craft is the pacing — the courses follow the laughter, not the clock. The Tuscan table's lesson: abundance is a feeling, not a budget — the full table matters more than the fancy plate. The harvest is the theme; the sharing is the feast.

Key points:
- Family-style platters build tablemates.
- Courses follow the laughter.
- Abundance is a feeling, not a budget.
- The sharing is the feast.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Tuscan Harvest Table

900111.title: The Midnight Ramen Bar
900111.description: Steam and slurp: the late-night ramen party.
900111.content:
The Midnight Ramen Bar — Steam and slurp: the late-night ramen party.

The midnight ramen bar serves steam at midnight: a build-your-own ramen station with rich broth, springy noodles, and a dozen toppings. The design key is the broth — make it long and deep, because the broth is the party. The setup is the bar: guests assemble their bowls, and the assembling is the entertainment. The hosting craft is the timing — the ramen lands when the evening needs its second wind. The ramen bar's lesson: the interactive meal is the theme — the guests cook their own joy. The steam is the atmosphere; the slurp is the applause.

Key points:
- The broth is the party.
- Build-your-own bar entertains.
- Time it for the second wind.
- Guests cook their own joy.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Midnight Ramen Bar

900112.title: The Parisian Bistro Night
900112.description: Small tables, big flavors: the bistro evening.
900112.content:
The Parisian Bistro Night — Small tables, big flavors: the bistro evening.

The Parisian bistro night is small tables and big flavors: onion soup, steak frites, and a chocolate mousse that ends all debate. The design key is the bistro format — small tables of four, the menu on a chalkboard, the courses unhurried. The atmosphere is the candlelight and the Edith Piaf — the room should feel like the 6th arrondissement. The hosting craft is the wine service — one good bottle per table, poured with ceremony. The bistro night's lesson: intimacy is the theme — the small table makes the big evening. The chalkboard is the menu; the candle is the light.

Key points:
- Small tables of four.
- Chalkboard menu, unhurried courses.
- One good bottle per table.
- Intimacy is the theme.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Parisian Bistro Night

900113.title: The Spice Route Feast
900113.description: Five cuisines, one table: the spice journey.
900113.content:
The Spice Route Feast — Five cuisines, one table: the spice journey.

The spice route feast journeys five cuisines in one evening: the dishes follow the old trade winds from pepper to saffron. The design key is the map — a printed spice route on the table, with each course marked at its port. The menu is the voyage: the starter in Kerala, the main in Persia, the dessert in Venice. The hosting craft is the tasting notes — a card per course, with the spice's story. The feast's lesson: the meal is a journey — the guests travel without leaving the table. The map is the menu; the spices are the miles.

Key points:
- Printed spice route on the table.
- Each course at its port of call.
- Tasting cards tell the spice stories.
- The meal is the journey.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Spice Route Feast

900114.title: The Farmhouse Long Table
900114.description: From the garden: the farmhouse dinner.
900114.content:
The Farmhouse Long Table — From the garden: the farmhouse dinner.

The farmhouse long table serves the garden: the menu is whatever's ripe, cooked simply, eaten together. The design key is the provenance — every dish names its source, and the guests taste the place. The format is the long table: one table, everyone, the food passed down the line. The hosting craft is the harvest — let the guests pick something before dinner. The farmhouse table's lesson: the season is the theme — the menu writes itself in the garden. The place is the flavor; the table is the community.

Key points:
- Menu from the ripe garden.
- Every dish names its source.
- Guests harvest before dinner.
- The season writes the menu.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Farmhouse Long Table

900115.title: The Sushi Master Evening
900115.description: Precision and ritual: the sushi night.
900115.content:
The Sushi Master Evening — Precision and ritual: the sushi night.

The sushi master evening is precision and ritual: the rice seasoned just so, the fish cut to order, the courses in the traditional sequence. The design key is the counter — seat the guests at the counter (or a counter-like bar) and serve piece by piece. The hosting craft is the education — the host narrates each piece: the fish, the cut, the why. The activity is the hand-roll round: guests make their own temaki to finish. The sushi night's lesson: ritual is the theme — the sequence is the ceremony. The counter is the stage; the piece is the performance.

Key points:
- Counter seating, piece-by-piece service.
- Narrate each piece: fish, cut, why.
- Hand-roll round to finish.
- Ritual is the theme.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Sushi Master Evening

900116.title: The Fireside Fondue Night
900116.description: Melted and merry: the fondue gathering.
900116.content:
The Fireside Fondue Night — Melted and merry: the fondue gathering.

The fireside fondue night is melted and merry: cheese, then chocolate, the pots bubbling at the table's center. The design key is the pot — the fondue pot is the hearth, and the table gathers around it. The menu is the dippers: bread, apples, and the adventurous (the pickle skeptics convert). The hosting craft is the rules — the lost-bread penalties, read aloud, make the game. The fondue night's lesson: the shared pot is the theme — everyone eats from the same fire. The pot is the hearth; the dippers are the democracy.

Key points:
- The pot is the hearth.
- Dippers: classics plus converts.
- Read the lost-bread rules aloud.
- The shared pot is the theme.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Fireside Fondue Night

900117.title: The Mediterranean Mezze Party
900117.description: Small plates, long evening: the mezze night.
900117.content:
The Mediterranean Mezze Party — Small plates, long evening: the mezze night.

The Mediterranean mezze night is small plates and a long evening: hummus, olives, grilled halloumi, and the table that never empties. The design key is the spread — the whole table covered at once, the guests grazing for hours. The format is the no-course dinner: everything out, no sequence, the evening finds its own rhythm. The hosting craft is the replenish — the host quietly refills, and the abundance never breaks. The mezze night's lesson: the graze is the theme — the evening is the meal. The table is the landscape; the night is the course.

Key points:
- The whole table covered at once.
- No courses: the evening finds its rhythm.
- Quiet replenishing keeps abundance.
- The graze is the theme.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Mediterranean Mezze Party

900118.title: The New Orleans Supper Club
900118.description: Jazz and gumbo: the supper club night.
900118.content:
The New Orleans Supper Club — Jazz and gumbo: the supper club night.

The New Orleans supper club is jazz and gumbo: the brass on the speaker, the roux on the stove, the evening with a second-line soul. The design key is the music — the playlist is the room's heartbeat, from Preservation Hall to the modern bounce. The menu is the trinity: gumbo, jambalaya, and the bread pudding that ends the night right. The hosting craft is the toast — the host raises the Sazerac and the room follows. The supper club's lesson: the spirit is the theme — laissez les bons temps rouler isn't a slogan, it's the seating chart. The jazz is the air; the gumbo is the ground.

Key points:
- The playlist is the heartbeat.
- The trinity: gumbo, jambalaya, bread pudding.
- The host's toast sets the spirit.
- The spirit is the seating chart.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The New Orleans Supper Club

900119.title: The Chef's Counter at Home
900119.description: The tasting menu, domesticated: the home counter.
900119.content:
The Chef's Counter at Home — The tasting menu, domesticated: the home counter.

The chef's counter at home domesticates the tasting menu: six courses, counter seating, the host cooking in front of the guests. The design key is the performance — the cooking is the show, so the kitchen must face the table. The menu is the progression: the courses build, the flavors arc, the finale lands. The hosting craft is the narration — the host plates and explains, course by course. The counter's lesson: the kitchen is the theme — the guests don't just eat the meal, they witness it. The counter is the stage; the tasting is the theater.

Key points:
- Cook facing the guests.
- Six courses with a flavor arc.
- Narrate every plating.
- The kitchen is the theater.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Chef's Counter at Home

900120.title: The Vendor Booking Calendar
900120.description: Who to book when: the vendor timeline.
900120.content:
The Vendor Booking Calendar — Who to book when: the vendor timeline.

The vendor booking calendar answers the planner's hardest question — who to book when. The timeline runs backwards from party day: the venue at twelve weeks, the caterer at eight, the photographer at six, the rentals at four, the cake at three. The design key is the dependency map: the caterer needs the venue's kitchen specs, the florist needs the table count, and the calendar encodes the order. The hosting craft is the confirmation cascade — confirm every vendor at two weeks, one week, and the day before. The calendar's lesson: the booking is the party's skeleton — get the order right and the flesh follows. The timeline is the truth.

Key points:
- Book backwards from party day.
- Encode vendor dependencies.
- Confirm at two weeks, one week, day-before.
- The booking order is the skeleton.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Vendor Booking Calendar

900121.title: The Contingency Playbook
900121.description: When the plan meets reality: the backup book.
900121.content:
The Contingency Playbook — When the plan meets reality: the backup book.

The contingency playbook is the party's insurance: the written plan for everything that can go wrong. The chapters are the classics — rain (the tent vendor on standby), the no-show vendor (the backup list), the power outage (the generator rental), the guest emergency (the first-aid kit and the plan). The design key is the trigger: each contingency names its tripwire — the forecast percentage, the confirmation deadline — so the decision is made before the crisis. The hosting craft is the calm: the playbook lets the host smile through the storm. The playbook's lesson: the backup plan is the real plan — the party that survives is the party that prepared. Hope for sun; book the tent.

Key points:
- Write the plan for every disaster.
- Name each contingency's trigger.
- Decide before the crisis.
- The backup plan is the real plan.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Contingency Playbook

900122.title: The Guest Experience Map
900122.description: The party through their eyes: the journey map.
900122.content:
The Guest Experience Map — The party through their eyes: the journey map.

The guest experience map charts the party through the guests' eyes: arrival, greeting, the first hour, the peak, the wind-down, the farewell. The design key is the arrival — the first ten minutes decide the night, so the entrance, the greeter, and the first drink are engineered. The map's middle is the energy arc: the host plans the peaks (the toast, the game, the surprise) and the valleys (the food, the breather). The hosting craft is the farewell — the goodnight must be as warm as the welcome. The map's lesson: the party is a story — the guest is the protagonist, and the host is the narrator. Map the journey; the guests live it.

Key points:
- Engineer the first ten minutes.
- Plan the energy arc: peaks and valleys.
- The farewell matches the welcome.
- The guest is the protagonist.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Guest Experience Map

900123.title: The Theme-to-Reality Pipeline
900123.description: From Pinterest board to party: the execution pipeline.
900123.content:
The Theme-to-Reality Pipeline — From Pinterest board to party: the execution pipeline.

The theme-to-reality pipeline converts inspiration into execution: the mood board becomes the shopping list, the list becomes the build schedule, the schedule becomes the party. The stages are capture (collect every idea), cull (keep the load-bearing ten percent), source (price the keepers), build (make or buy), and stage (install before the guests). The design key is the cull — the pipeline's ruthlessness is its value, because the theme dies under too many ideas. The hosting craft is the budget gate: every kept idea gets a price before it gets a place. The pipeline's lesson: the theme is a supply chain — manage it like one. The board is the dream; the pipeline is the party.

Key points:
- Stages: capture, cull, source, build, stage.
- Cull ruthlessly: keep ten percent.
- Price every idea before placing it.
- The theme is a supply chain.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Theme-to-Reality Pipeline

900124.title: The Party Debrief Ritual
900124.description: After the last guest: learning from the night.
900124.content:
The Party Debrief Ritual — After the last guest: learning from the night.

The party debrief ritual harvests the night's lessons: the morning after, the host writes what worked, what broke, and what to steal for next time. The format is the three lists — keep, fix, steal — written while the memory is fresh. The design key is the honesty: the debrief is private, so the host can admit the playlist died and the cake saved the night. The hosting craft is the guest feedback — the casual 'what was your favorite part' texts, collected, not surveyed. The ritual's lesson: the party is a prototype — every edition teaches the next. The debrief is the tuition; the next party is the degree.

Key points:
- Write the debrief the morning after.
- Three lists: keep, fix, steal.
- Collect favorites casually, not by survey.
- Every party prototypes the next.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Party Debrief Ritual

900125.title: The Multi-Day Celebration Plan
900125.description: The weekend, not the evening: the festival plan.
900125.content:
The Multi-Day Celebration Plan — The weekend, not the evening: the festival plan.

The multi-day celebration plan stretches the party across the weekend: the welcome night, the main event, the recovery brunch — a festival, not an evening. The design key is the arc: each day has its own energy, building to the main event and easing into the farewell. The logistics are the lodging: the plan houses the out-of-towners, feeds the stayers, and schedules the downtime. The hosting craft is the stamina — the host plans their own rest, because the weekend is a marathon. The plan's lesson: the celebration is the container — the weekend holds the moments the evening can't. The arc is the art; the rest is the craft.

Key points:
- Arc the weekend: welcome, peak, farewell.
- House and feed the stayers.
- Plan the host's rest too.
- The weekend holds what evenings can't.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Multi-Day Celebration Plan

900126.title: The Surprise Party Protocol
900126.description: The secret, kept: the surprise playbook.
900126.content:
The Surprise Party Protocol — The secret, kept: the surprise playbook.

The surprise party protocol keeps the secret: the compartmentalized guest list, the decoy plan, and the reveal choreography. The design key is the information discipline — the guest of honor hears nothing, which means the invitations never mention the venue aloud. The logistics are the decoy: the cover story must be boring enough to believe. The hosting craft is the reveal — the lights, the shout, the moment, rehearsed. The protocol's lesson: the surprise is a heist — the crew, the plan, the getaway (the guest of honor's shock). The secret is the gift; the party is the wrapping.

Key points:
- Information discipline: the honoree hears nothing.
- The decoy must be boringly believable.
- Rehearse the reveal moment.
- The surprise is a heist.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Surprise Party Protocol

900127.title: The Cultural Celebration Guide
900127.description: Honoring traditions well: the respectful celebration.
900127.content:
The Cultural Celebration Guide — Honoring traditions well: the respectful celebration.

The cultural celebration guide helps hosts honor traditions well: the research, the consultation, and the humility to ask. The design key is the source — learn from the tradition's bearers, not from the internet's approximations. The hosting craft is the invitation: invite the community in, don't perform the culture at them. The menu, the music, the ritual — each gets its proper context, explained with respect. The guide's lesson: the celebration is a guesthood — the host is the guest of the tradition. Honor, don't appropriate. The respect is the theme.

Key points:
- Learn from the tradition's bearers.
- Invite the community in.
- Give every element its proper context.
- The host is the tradition's guest.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Cultural Celebration Guide

900128.title: The Accessibility Checklist
900128.description: Every guest, fully welcome: the access audit.
900128.content:
The Accessibility Checklist — Every guest, fully welcome: the access audit.

The accessibility checklist audits the party for every guest: the step-free entrance, the quiet room, the labeled food, the accessible restroom. The design key is the ask — invite access needs on the RSVP, plainly and without fuss. The checklist's chapters are mobility, sensory, dietary, and social: the ramp, the volume, the allergens, the alone-together space. The hosting craft is the normalizing — the access features are just part of the plan, announced like the parking. The checklist's lesson: the welcome is the theme — the party is only as good as its least-welcomed guest. Audit the welcome; the party follows.

Key points:
- Ask access needs on the RSVP.
- Chapters: mobility, sensory, dietary, social.
- Normalize: announce access like parking.
- The least-welcomed guest sets the grade.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Accessibility Checklist

900129.title: The Legacy Party Album
900129.description: The night, remembered: the album system.
900129.content:
The Legacy Party Album — The night, remembered: the album system.

The legacy party album preserves the night: the photo system that actually gets used, curated, and kept. The design key is the capture — the shared album link, the disposable cameras on the tables, the designated photographer for the key moments. The curation is the week-after ritual: the host picks the hundred best and deletes the rest. The hosting craft is the sharing — the album goes to every guest, because the memories are communal. The album's lesson: the party's second life is the record — the night ends, the album compounds. The photos are the encore. Keep the encore.

Key points:
- Shared album link plus table cameras.
- Curate the week after: keep the hundred.
- Share the album with every guest.
- The record is the party's second life.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Legacy Party Album

JAH-PARTY-000068.title: The Time Traveler's Ball
JAH-PARTY-000068.description: Every era, one room: the time-travel theme.
JAH-PARTY-000068.content:
The Time Traveler's Ball — Every era, one room: the time-travel theme.

The time traveler's ball invites every era to one room: guests dress from any century, and the party becomes a collision of histories. - Costume clues drive the era quiz.
- The timeline arch sets the entrance.
- Themes are frameworks, not costumes.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Time Traveler's Ball

JAH-PARTY-000069.title: The Neon Noir Night
JAH-PARTY-000069.description: Detective shadows in neon: the noir party.
JAH-PARTY-000069.content:
The Neon Noir Night — Detective shadows in neon: the noir party.

The neon noir night is detective fiction with the lights turned electric: fedoras and trench coats under blacklight, the case file as the evening's game. The design key is the lighting — blacklight, neon tape, and fog turn any room into a 1940s fever dream. The game is the case: teams get evidence envelopes and thirty minutes to name the culprit. JAH-PARTY-000075.title: The Hollywood Premiere
JAH-PARTY-000075.description: Red carpet and flashbulbs: the premiere party.
JAH-PARTY-000075.content:
The Hollywood Premiere — Red carpet and flashbulbs: the premiere party.

JAH-PARTY-000076.title: The Pirate Cove Party
JAH-PARTY-000076.description: X marks the spot: the pirate bash.

JAH-PARTY-000077.title: The Space Station Soirée
JAH-PARTY-000077.description: Zero gravity, full elegance: the orbital party.
JAH-PARTY-000077.content:
The Space Station Soirée — Zero gravity, full elegance: the orbital party.

The space station soirée hosts the party in orbit: silver and starlight, freeze-dried hors d'oeuvres, and a mission patch for every guest. JAH-PARTY-000078.title: The Tuscan Harvest Table
JAH-PARTY-000078.description: Rustic abundance: the Tuscan dinner party.
JAH-PARTY-000078.content:
The Tuscan Harvest Table — Rustic abundance: the Tuscan dinner party.

The Tuscan harvest table is rustic abundance: a long wooden table, family-style platters, and wine that doesn't need a special occasion. - The sharing is the feast.

JAH-PARTY-000080.title: The Parisian Bistro Night
JAH-PARTY-000080.description: Small tables, big flavors: the bistro evening.

The bistro night's lesson: intimacy is the theme — the small table makes the big evening. The chalkboard is the menu; the candle is the light.

- One good bottle per table.
- Intimacy is the theme.

JAH-PARTY-000081.description: Five cuisines, one table: the spice journey.

JAH-PARTY-000082.description: From the garden: the farmhouse dinner.

The farmhouse long table serves the garden: the menu is whatever's ripe, cooked simply, eaten together. The design key is the provenance — every dish names its source, and the guests taste the place. The farmhouse table's lesson: the season is the theme — the menu writes itself in the garden. The place is the flavor; the table is the community.

- The season writes the menu.

JAH-PARTY-000083.title: The Sushi Master Evening
JAH-PARTY-000083.description: Precision and ritual: the sushi night.

- Hand-roll round to finish.

JAH-PARTY-000084.title: The Fireside Fondue Night

JAH-PARTY-000085.title: The Mediterranean Mezze Party
JAH-PARTY-000085.description: Small plates, long evening: the mezze night.

The Mediterranean Mezze Party — Small plates, long evening: the mezze night.

The Mediterranean mezze night is small plates and a long evening: hummus, olives, grilled halloumi, and the table that never empties. - The graze is the theme.

JAH-PARTY-000086.title: The New Orleans Supper Club
JAH-PARTY-000086.description: Jazz and gumbo: the supper club night.
JAH-PARTY-000086.content:
The New Orleans Supper Club — Jazz and gumbo: the supper club night.

The New Orleans supper club is jazz and gumbo: the brass on the speaker, the roux on the stove, the evening with a second-line soul. The design key is the music — the playlist is the room's heartbeat, from Preservation Hall to the modern bounce. The Chef's Counter at Home — The tasting menu, domesticated: the home counter.

The chef's counter at home domesticates the tasting menu: six courses, counter seating, the host cooking in front of the guests. The design key is the performance — the cooking is the show, so the kitchen must face the table. The menu is the progression: the courses build, the flavors arc, the finale lands. The hosting craft is the narration — the host plates and explains, course by course. The counter's lesson: the kitchen is the theme — the guests don't just eat the meal, they witness it. JAH-PARTY-000088.title: The Vendor Booking Calendar
JAH-PARTY-000088.description: Who to book when: the vendor timeline.
JAH-PARTY-000088.content:
The Vendor Booking Calendar — Who to book when: the vendor timeline.

The vendor booking calendar answers the planner's hardest question — who to book when. The timeline runs backwards from party day: the venue at twelve weeks, the caterer at eight, the photographer at six, the rentals at four, the cake at three. The design key is the dependency map: the caterer needs the venue's kitchen specs, the florist needs the table count, and the calendar encodes the order. The hosting craft is the confirmation cascade — confirm every vendor at two weeks, one week, and the day before. The calendar's lesson: the booking is the party's skeleton — get the order right and the flesh follows. The timeline is the truth.

Key points:
- Book backwards from party day.
- Encode vendor dependencies.
- Confirm at two weeks, one week, day-before.
- The booking order is the skeleton.

JAH-PARTY-000089.title: The Contingency Playbook
JAH-PARTY-000089.description: When the plan meets reality: the backup book.
JAH-PARTY-000089.content:
The Contingency Playbook — When the plan meets reality: the backup book.

The contingency playbook is the party's insurance: the written plan for everything that can go wrong. The chapters are the classics — rain (the tent vendor on standby), the no-show vendor (the backup list), the power outage (the generator rental), the guest emergency (the first-aid kit and the plan). The design key is the trigger: each contingency names its tripwire — the forecast percentage, the confirmation deadline — so the decision is made before the crisis. The hosting craft is the calm: the playbook lets the host smile through the storm. The playbook's lesson: the backup plan is the real plan — the party that survives is the party that prepared. Hope for sun; book the tent.

Key points:
- Write the plan for every disaster.
- Name each contingency's trigger.
- Decide before the crisis.
- The backup plan is the real plan.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Contingency Playbook

JAH-PARTY-000090.title: The Guest Experience Map
JAH-PARTY-000090.description: The party through their eyes: the journey map.
JAH-PARTY-000090.content:
The Guest Experience Map — The party through their eyes: the journey map.

The guest experience map charts the party through the guests' eyes: arrival, greeting, the first hour, the peak, the wind-down, the farewell. The design key is the arrival — the first ten minutes decide the night, so the entrance, the greeter, and the first drink are engineered. The map's middle is the energy arc: the host plans the peaks (the toast, the game, the surprise) and the valleys (the food, the breather). The hosting craft is the farewell — the goodnight must be as warm as the welcome. The map's lesson: the party is a story — the guest is the protagonist, and the host is the narrator. Map the journey; the guests live it.

Key points:
- Engineer the first ten minutes.
- Plan the energy arc: peaks and valleys.
- The farewell matches the welcome.
- The guest is the protagonist.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Guest Experience Map

JAH-PARTY-000091.title: The Theme-to-Reality Pipeline
JAH-PARTY-000091.description: From Pinterest board to party: the execution pipeline.
JAH-PARTY-000091.content:
The Theme-to-Reality Pipeline — From Pinterest board to party: the execution pipeline.

The theme-to-reality pipeline converts inspiration into execution: the mood board becomes the shopping list, the list becomes the build schedule, the schedule becomes the party. The stages are capture (collect every idea), cull (keep the load-bearing ten percent), source (price the keepers), build (make or buy), and stage (install before the guests). The design key is the cull — the pipeline's ruthlessness is its value, because the theme dies under too many ideas. The hosting craft is the budget gate: every kept idea gets a price before it gets a place. The pipeline's lesson: the theme is a supply chain — manage it like one. The board is the dream; the pipeline is the party.

Key points:
- Stages: capture, cull, source, build, stage.
- Cull ruthlessly: keep ten percent.
- Price every idea before placing it.
- The theme is a supply chain.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Theme-to-Reality Pipeline

JAH-PARTY-000092.title: The Party Debrief Ritual
JAH-PARTY-000092.description: After the last guest: learning from the night.
JAH-PARTY-000092.content:
The Party Debrief Ritual — After the last guest: learning from the night.

The party debrief ritual harvests the night's lessons: the morning after, the host writes what worked, what broke, and what to steal for next time. The format is the three lists — keep, fix, steal — written while the memory is fresh. The design key is the honesty: the debrief is private, so the host can admit the playlist died and the cake saved the night. The hosting craft is the guest feedback — the casual 'what was your favorite part' texts, collected, not surveyed. The ritual's lesson: the party is a prototype — every edition teaches the next. The debrief is the tuition; the next party is the degree.

Key points:
- Write the debrief the morning after.
- Three lists: keep, fix, steal.
- Collect favorites casually, not by survey.
- Every party prototypes the next.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Party Debrief Ritual

JAH-PARTY-000093.title: The Multi-Day Celebration Plan
JAH-PARTY-000093.description: The weekend, not the evening: the festival plan.
JAH-PARTY-000093.content:
The Multi-Day Celebration Plan — The weekend, not the evening: the festival plan.

The multi-day celebration plan stretches the party across the weekend: the welcome night, the main event, the recovery brunch — a festival, not an evening. The design key is the arc: each day has its own energy, building to the main event and easing into the farewell. The logistics are the lodging: the plan houses the out-of-towners, feeds the stayers, and schedules the downtime. The hosting craft is the stamina — the host plans their own rest, because the weekend is a marathon. The plan's lesson: the celebration is the container — the weekend holds the moments the evening can't. The arc is the art; the rest is the craft.

Key points:
- Arc the weekend: welcome, peak, farewell.
- House and feed the stayers.
- Plan the host's rest too.
- The weekend holds what evenings can't.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Multi-Day Celebration Plan

JAH-PARTY-000094.title: The Surprise Party Protocol
JAH-PARTY-000094.description: The secret, kept: the surprise playbook.
JAH-PARTY-000094.content:
The Surprise Party Protocol — The secret, kept: the surprise playbook.

The surprise party protocol keeps the secret: the compartmentalized guest list, the decoy plan, and the reveal choreography. The design key is the information discipline — the guest of honor hears nothing, which means the invitations never mention the venue aloud. The logistics are the decoy: the cover story must be boring enough to believe. The hosting craft is the reveal — the lights, the shout, the moment, rehearsed. The protocol's lesson: the surprise is a heist — the crew, the plan, the getaway (the guest of honor's shock). The secret is the gift; the party is the wrapping.

Key points:
- Information discipline: the honoree hears nothing.
- The decoy must be boringly believable.
- Rehearse the reveal moment.
- The surprise is a heist.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Surprise Party Protocol

JAH-PARTY-000095.title: The Cultural Celebration Guide
JAH-PARTY-000095.description: Honoring traditions well: the respectful celebration.
JAH-PARTY-000095.content:
The Cultural Celebration Guide — Honoring traditions well: the respectful celebration.

The cultural celebration guide helps hosts honor traditions well: the research, the consultation, and the humility to ask. The design key is the source — learn from the tradition's bearers, not from the internet's approximations. The hosting craft is the invitation: invite the community in, don't perform the culture at them. The menu, the music, the ritual — each gets its proper context, explained with respect. The guide's lesson: the celebration is a guesthood — the host is the guest of the tradition. Honor, don't appropriate. The respect is the theme.

Key points:
- Learn from the tradition's bearers.
- Invite the community in.
- Give every element its proper context.
- The host is the tradition's guest.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Cultural Celebration Guide

JAH-PARTY-000096.title: The Accessibility Checklist
JAH-PARTY-000096.description: Every guest, fully welcome: the access audit.
JAH-PARTY-000096.content:
The Accessibility Checklist — Every guest, fully welcome: the access audit.

The accessibility checklist audits the party for every guest: the step-free entrance, the quiet room, the labeled food, the accessible restroom. The design key is the ask — invite access needs on the RSVP, plainly and without fuss. The checklist's chapters are mobility, sensory, dietary, and social: the ramp, the volume, the allergens, the alone-together space. The hosting craft is the normalizing — the access features are just part of the plan, announced like the parking. The checklist's lesson: the welcome is the theme — the party is only as good as its least-welcomed guest. Audit the welcome; the party follows.

Key points:
- Ask access needs on the RSVP.
- Chapters: mobility, sensory, dietary, social.
- Normalize: announce access like parking.
- The least-welcomed guest sets the grade.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Accessibility Checklist

JAH-PARTY-000097.title: The Legacy Party Album
JAH-PARTY-000097.description: The night, remembered: the album system.
JAH-PARTY-000097.content:
The Legacy Party Album — The night, remembered: the album system.

The legacy party album preserves the night: the photo system that actually gets used, curated, and kept. The design key is the capture — the shared album link, the disposable cameras on the tables, the designated photographer for the key moments. The curation is the week-after ritual: the host picks the hundred best and deletes the rest. The hosting craft is the sharing — the album goes to every guest, because the memories are communal. The album's lesson: the party's second life is the record — the night ends, the album compounds. The photos are the encore. Keep the encore.

- Shared album link plus table cameras.
- Curate the week after: keep the hundred.
- Share the album with every guest.
- The record is the party's second life.
